title: The わけ Family: わけだ, わけではない, わけがない, わけにはいかない
description: Four look-alike patterns with very different meanings: no wonder, it's not that, no way, and can't afford to.

points.title: 〜わけだ: no wonder, that's why
points.summary: Plain form + わけだ = a logical conclusion: 'so that's why / no wonder'. Nouns take の/な (学生なわけだ), な-adj take な.
points.body:
わけ means 'reason, logic'. **わけだ** draws the natural conclusion from facts you just learned:
- 毎日3時間も練習しているのか。上手な**わけだ** (No wonder he's good.)
- 10年もアメリカにいた。英語がペラペラな**わけだ**.

**Attachment:** plain form; な-adj + な; nouns + な/の (学生な**わけ**).

**わけだ vs はずだ:** はずだ predicts what *should* be true; わけだ explains something you *already see* ('that explains it').
examples: {毎日|まいにち}3{時間|じかん}も{練習|れんしゅう}しているのか。{上手|じょうず}なわけだ。
He practises 3 hours a day? No wonder he's good.

points.title: 〜わけではない: it's not that …, it doesn't mean that
points.summary: Plain form + わけではない = partial denial: 'it's not (exactly) that …'.
points.body:
- 日本料理が嫌いな**わけではない**が、今日は食べたくない (It's not that I dislike Japanese food, but…).
- お金がない**わけではない** (it's not that I have no money).

Often with **別に** / **必ずしも** and followed by が/けど. Casual: わけじゃない.
examples: {日本料理|にほんりょうり}が{嫌|きら}いなわけではないが、{今日|きょう}は{食|た}べたくない。
It's not that I dislike Japanese food, but I don't want it today.

points.title: 〜わけがない: there's no way that …
points.summary: Plain form + わけがない = strong denial: 'impossible, can't be'. Casual: わけない.
points.body:
- あんなに練習したんだから、負ける**わけがない** (there's no way we'll lose).
- 彼が嘘をつく**わけがない**.

Very similar to **はずがない**; わけがない sounds a bit more emotional/colloquial.
examples: {彼|かれ}が{嘘|うそ}をつくわけがない。
There's no way he would lie.

points.title: 〜わけにはいかない: can't (afford to), must not
points.summary: Dictionary form + わけにはいかない = can't do it because of social/moral reasons. ない-form + わけにはいかない = must do.
points.body:
- 明日は大事な試験があるから、休む**わけにはいかない** (I can't afford to take a day off).
- 友達の結婚式だから、行か**ないわけにはいかない** (I can't *not* go → I must go).

The 'can't' comes from circumstances or obligation, not from physical inability (that would be 〜られない).
examples: {明日|あした}は{大事|だいじ}な{試験|しけん}があるから、{休|やす}むわけにはいかない。
I have an important exam tomorrow, so I can't afford to skip.
{友達|ともだち}の{結婚式|けっこんしき}だから、{行|い}かないわけにはいかない。
It's my friend's wedding, so I have to go.

questions.prompt: {毎日|まいにち}3{時間|じかん}も{練習|れんしゅう}しているのか。{上手|じょうず}な（　）だ。
notes: わけでだ isn't grammatical.
わけがだ isn't grammatical.
わけにだ isn't grammatical.
questions.translation: He practises 3 hours a day? No wonder he's good.

questions.prompt: {彼|かれ}は10{年|ねん}もアメリカにいた。{英語|えいご}がペラペラな（　）。
questions.explanation: Ten years in America → the logical conclusion: **わけだ**.
notes: わけではない ('it's not that …') denies the obvious conclusion.
わけがない ('no way') contradicts ten years in America.
わけにはいかない ('can't afford to') makes no sense here.
questions.translation: He lived in America for 10 years — no wonder his English is fluent.

questions.prompt: {日本料理|にほんりょうり}が{嫌|きら}いな（　）が、{今日|きょう}は{食|た}べたくない。
questions.explanation: Partial denial + が: **わけではない**.
notes: わけがない ('no way I dislike it') + が is odd here.
わけにはいかない doesn't fit 嫌い.
わけだ ('that's why I dislike it') contradicts the が-clause.
questions.translation: It's not that I dislike Japanese food, but I don't want it today.

questions.prompt: What does 「お{金|かね}がないわけではない」 mean?
options: There's no way I have no money.
It's not that I don't have money.
No wonder I have no money.
I can't afford to have no money.
questions.explanation: わけではない = partial denial.
notes: That's ないわけがない.
That's ないわけだ.
That's ないわけにはいかない.

questions.prompt: あんなに{練習|れんしゅう}したんだから、{負|ま}ける（　）。
notes: わけではない = 'it's not that we'll lose' — not the strong denial.
わけだ = 'no wonder we lose' — contradicts all that practice.
わけで leaves the sentence unfinished.
questions.translation: We practised so much — there's no way we'll lose.

notes: わけがある = 'there's a reason' — not a denial.
わけはなく can't end the sentence.
わけをない isn't grammatical.
questions.translation: There's no way he would lie.

questions.prompt: {明日|あした}は{大事|だいじ}な{試験|しけん}があるから、{休|やす}む（　）。
questions.explanation: Can't afford to: **わけにはいかない**.
notes: いかなく can't end the sentence.
The particle is に, not で.
いる isn't part of the pattern.
questions.translation: I have an important exam tomorrow, so I can't afford to skip.

questions.prompt: （I have to go.）{友達|ともだち}の{結婚式|けっこんしき}だから、{行|い}か（　）。
options: なくわけにはいかない
ないわけにはいかない
questions.explanation: ない + わけにはいかない = can't *not* do → must.
notes: なく isn't the right form — use ない.
いく — the pattern is negative: いかない.
いかなく can't end the sentence.
questions.translation: It's my friend's wedding, so I have to go.

questions.prompt: {寝坊|ねぼう}したのか。それで{遅刻|ちこく}した（　）。
questions.explanation: Explaining what you see: **わけだ** (so that's why).
notes: わけにはいかない ('can't afford to') doesn't fit.
わけではない ('it's not that…') doesn't fit.
わけがない ('no way') contradicts the oversleeping.
questions.translation: You overslept? So that's why you were late.

questions.prompt: {嫌|きら}いな（　）けど、あまり{行|い}きたくない。
notes: わけだけど contradicts the second half.
わけにはいかない doesn't go with 嫌い.
わけがないけど = 'there's no way I dislike it, but' — odd.
questions.translation: It's not that I dislike it, but I don't really want to go.

questions.prompt: こんな{難|むずか}しい{問題|もんだい}、{子供|こども}に{解|と}ける（　）。
notes: わけで can't end the sentence.
わけに can't end the sentence.
わけだ = 'no wonder a child can solve it' — contradicts 難しい.
questions.translation: There's no way a child could solve such a hard problem.

questions.prompt: {先生|せんせい}に{頼|たの}まれたので、{断|ことわ}る（　）。
questions.explanation: Can't refuse (social reasons): **わけにはいかない**.
notes: いかなく can't end the sentence.
いる isn't part of the pattern.
The particle is に, not で.
questions.translation: My teacher asked me, so I can't really refuse.
